title: 1980 AHSME Problem 5
statement: If \(AB\) and \(CD\) are perpendicular diameters of circle \(Q,\) \(P\) in \(AQ,\) and \(\angle QPC=60^\circ,\) then the length of \(PQ\) divided by the length of \(AQ\) is

solutions.text:
Triangle \(PQC\) is right at \(Q\) and has \(\angle P=60^\circ,\) so it is a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle. Since \(QC=AQ,\) \[ \frac{PQ}{AQ}=\frac{PQ}{QC}=\frac1{\sqrt3} =\frac{\sqrt3}{3}. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use the perpendicular diameters to identify a right angle in \(\triangle PQC\)
Relate the short and long legs of the resulting \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle
